prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of GLP-1 and the identification of its active form, which made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-achievement B021 prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange tested it and it held on the science, not on the opening tally. The causal chain is complete and each link has a named owner in the trio: human incretin physiology (Holst), proglucagon processing and receptor biology (Drucker), and the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov). Independent outcome trials across several drug classes show glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal effects, so neither maturity nor interpretation is in doubt. No other shortlisted achievement combines that clarity of mechanism with demonstrated benefit at this scale, and a second part would only force a smaller B021 group without improving the case.
statement.case_against: The reservations are real and I have not argued them away. First, the Mojsov versus Habener priority for the active truncated peptide cannot be settled from the supplied record, and Habener is not among the credited names. Second, the three-person cap leaves Knudsen out, so a physiology prize does not recognise the long-acting analogues that reached patients. Third, every alternative has a comparable or harder credit problem: Eshhar for B033, a six-way split for B044, and upstream TNF and antibody work for B032. The strongest argument against my position is that the committee may prefer a prize for the therapy, and I do not think this configuration answers that preference.

responses.point: The chair asks whether the therapeutic step must be recognised and, if so, whether Knudsen or Mojsov yields, and wants round 2 to test whether four members accept a physiology-centred citation.
responses.response: I accept the physiology-centred citation and I would state openly that it is a deliberate choice, not an oversight. If the committee instead decided that the therapy is the achievement, Mojsov is the name that would be exposed, but I would not make that swap by default. Mojsov's contribution is the identification of the active peptide that every later drug targets, and a priority dispute is a reason to word the citation carefully, not a reason to replace her with a development role. I therefore keep the trio and propose the citation as written, which claims the physiology and the active form without a priority claim over the whole field.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius sees the Mojsov priority question as a risk to the configuration, not a reason to change the achievement, and would hold CAR-T and optogenetics to the same clarity-of-credit standard.
responses.response: I agree with that framing and with applying one standard to every candidate. By that standard B021 is the least exposed: the dispute concerns one of three roles. For B033 the exclusion of Eshhar and the Rosenberg question undermine the credited set, and for B044 any three of six names misrepresent priority. I also note that you describe me as proposing June, Sadelain and Rosenberg for CAR-T. My round-1 file does not support Rosenberg for a single-achievement prize, and I would not add him to reach three. I share your hesitation about long-term safety, but I weigh the missing Eshhar credit more heavily than maturity, and I still keep B033 as an alternative rather than a second part.

responses.point: Linnarsson keeps Knudsen out because the prize concerns the discovery that made the drug class possible and including her would reopen the physiology versus development line for every shortlisted candidate, while calling B033 an equally clear and arguably more novel modality.
responses.response: I agree on Knudsen, and the precedent argument persuades me more than it did in round 1: crediting drug development in B021 would force the committee to apply that line to B033, B042 and B032 as well. I do not agree that CAR-T is equally clear. A new therapeutic modality is a strong claim, but the receptor concept originates with Eshhar, who is outside the supplied names, so a June and Sadelain pair would credit the clinical translation of someone else's design. That is a harder attribution problem than the one in B021, and it is why I keep B033 behind it, though I would take it up first if the committee wants a second achievement.

responses.point: El-Manira holds that optogenetics is the better-reaching mature field and, in round 1, argued against ranking the UPR above it, while preferring Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann over Boyden, Deisseroth and Hegemann.
responses.response: I agree that B044 has the wider reach, but reach is not the same as a clean prize. Your revised Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann set is more defensible than the earlier set because it keeps the channelrhodopsin discoverers, yet it still leaves Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenbock unrecognised, and the discovery-versus-implementation split is a substantive choice about what is being rewarded. That leaves B044 as a methods prize with a contested allocation, which is why it stays an alternative for me. I have no better account of the split than you do, and I do not think it justifies delaying B021.

uncertainties: Whether the supplied record can settle Mojsov versus Habener for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, and whether four members accept a citation that does not take a position on that priority.
Whether the committee regards leaving out Knudsen and drug development as acceptable, since it rests on a policy judgement and not a scientific finding.
Whether a CAR-T prize can be fair without Eshhar, and whether a second part is warranted at all.
My recollection of GLP-1 and CAR-T priority details is not independently verified against primary sources.
statement.conflict_note: No recusal-level conflict for any shortlisted ballot. I co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen, neither of whom is a candidate, and share Karolinska Institutet affiliation with them. My single-cell and RNA-processing research is topically close to B042 (SMN2 splicing), with no documented tie to Krainer or Bennett, and B042 is not in my preferred configuration or alternatives. Nothing in round 1 changes this disclosure.
